correctness.rationale: The metric is reconstructed from Euclidean strip lifts: the nearest deck images in the two parity classes are at horizontal offsets t and 2s-t, leading to A and B. The (Y−Yʹ,Y+Yʹ) change of variables gives a diamond with constant density 1/(8h²). Integrating the event B≤r<A proves the exact CDF gap and strict interval; matched asymptotic scalings give coefficients 2√2/(3h√s) and R³/(48h⁴s²). Integrating the product of two unit uniforms gives both aspect-ratio probability branches, and explicit derivatives establish C² but not C³. Every step holds for all L,h>0. Exact-rational lift comparisons (7,203), seeded comparisons (750,009), asymptotic tests (12) and transition tests (4) passed from the included verifier. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove universal quantifiers; these are discharged analytically.

value.rationale: The comparison holds uniformly over every positive aspect ratio for two compact locally Euclidean surfaces with the same area and total boundary length but different topology. It identifies a complete stochastic order and its exact support, noninteger and integer sharp onset/terminal exponents, and a dimensionless coupling law with a C²/non-C³ aspect-ratio threshold. These results distinguish full distance geometry beyond moments or diameter and provide a tractable benchmark for boundary- and topology-sensitive distance distribution problems, without reliance on arbitrary parameter slices or negligible numerical improvements. The inherited cylinder tail is used only as a benchmark; the new value is the Möbius-versus-cylinder excess law and strictly ordered coupling.
